handled_verified._description: Analyzer-referenced node types (F1 PASS refs=15 unknown=0 at CLJ1; RE-MEASURED 2026-09-28 at FULL EXTENT by script/m14/tmp/clj-deep-audit.ts over 4,252 metabase Clojure files: 35 distinct node types observed, every one classified, 0 unclassified, 0 placeholder symbol names, 0 empty symbol names, and exactly 1 file with an ERROR node (0.024%) — that file contains 3 literal NUL bytes in a string literal, which no Clojure grammar can lex, so it is a corpus data artifact and is disclosed as such rather than counted as a parse defect). Behavior probe-verified 2019-06..2026-09 against the pinned wasm (@yogthos 0.0.14, the wasm-packaged sogaiu lineage) via real-clojure-analyzer.ts and the CLJ1 + CLJ-F5 + CLJ-ADV + M60-deep fixture batteries (42 fixtures, 63 mutants caught). sym_lit carries the name/namespace FIELDS (sym_name/sym_ns children) so those children are read through the field API, not type-matched — and since CLJ-D28 the qualified-name resolution reads those fields too, so no code path splits a symbol's text on `/`.

internal_silent._description: Traversal-transparent wrappers and literals verified by the shape probe (script/tmp-clj-shapes.ts, 2026-09-19) and the 142-file corpus census: each either carries no symbol/edge/complexity semantics, or its CHILDREN are walked generically (read-cond bodies, containers), and the wrapper itself correctly emits nothing. sym_name/sym_ns/kwd_name/kwd_ns are field children read via symName/childForFieldName — their text is consumed without type branches.

gap._description: CLJ1 (2026-09-19) closed C1-C13. The CLJ-F5 certification then found three further defect classes, and the CLJ-ADV adversarial review sixteen more — the claim 'no gaps' was falsified twice on the SAME surface, and each time because the instrument list was too small. THE M60 DEEP ROUND (2026-09-28) falsified it a THIRD time, and this time the falsifying instrument was not a differential at all. F5 compares the analyzer against `deriveClojureEdges`, and the two MIRROR each other's rules deliberately — so a defect present in BOTH is invisible by construction, and the lane's largest single defect was exactly that: `CLOJURE_CORE_BUILTINS` was a 437-name hand transcription that the oracle IMPORTS by reference, so every name it omitted was a MIRRORED fabrication. Measured: 2,525 `calls` edges to real clojure.core vars in the clojure corpus (30% of all 8,391 call edges), 999 in clj-kondo, 151 in core.async. The instruments that found it were four NEW ones, and the list grew again for the same reason it grew twice before: (1) script/m14/tmp/clj-core-derive.ts — DERIVE the language's own constant from clojure/clojure's source with the pinned wasm (namespace-scoped, top-level-only, privacy-filtered) and diff it against what ships; (2) script/m14/tmp/clj-core-impact.ts — count the emitted edges that name a derived core var; (3) script/m14/tmp/clj-gate-census.ts — for every SURVIVING core-named call, decide independently (file-declares / region-bound / referred / RESIDUAL) which exemption admitted it, so the claim 'every one is explained' is measured rather than asserted; (4) script/m14/tmp/clj-full-f5.ts — the F5 comparison at FULL EXTENT, sharded, because one wasm module cannot hold 4,122 metabase files (the W11 heap cliff), which is where the `h2x//` qualified-name defect surfaced (2 unexplained of 239,192 truth edges over 4,252 files) after a 60-file draw had missed it for a full wave. THE CLAIM NOW READS: no gap is known to any instrument built so far — and the instrument list is recorded here precisely because that claim has now broken three times, each break being the reason a fourth instrument existed. MEASURED RESIDUES, named rather than rounded: unshadowed core-call edges 6 / 11 / 2 (clojure / clj-kondo / core.async) with 0 RESIDUAL after independent classification; metabase 4,252 files 100% coverage MISSING=0 unexplained=0; clojure 143 files 6,871/6,871, clj-kondo 444 files 8,087/8,087, core.async 46 files 2,108/2,108. STILL OPEN, with sizes: multi-arity parameter merging (W23-c, registered; 342 sites in the three small corpora) needs a cross-lane `UniversalSymbol.parameters` decision; `:refer :all` names a whole lib and so registers no individual name (25 sites, documented — the `[*]` items path is the honest reading).
gap._relationship_class_wave: F5 compared FOUR of the seven relationship labels the clojure analyzer emits. `uses` and `contains` were excluded with a documented reason and therefore had no gate at all. `script/m14/clojure-truth.ts` derives both from the tree, and both are now at zero residual in every direction: uses truth=2650 emitted=2650 covered=100.00% MISSED=0 FABRICATED=0; contains minimum=6145 emitted=7762 covered=100.00% MISSED=0; owner audit 0 not-a-symbol / 0 not-spanning; contains consistency 0 target-missing / 0 line-wrong / 0 duplicated. On metabase (4,253 files) uses is 100.00% 0/0 and contains 100.00% with 2 residuals, both the same shape and recorded rather than papered over: the truth binds the HEAD's own name where a `^:parallel` metadata form sits in the name position on a `deftest` nested under a second `^{…}` wrapper (test/metabase/sql_tools/{macaw,sqlglot}/references_test.clj). The gate is proven able to fail: `--prove` runs ten negative proofs and all ten fire. The remaining four labels (`references`, `instantiates`, `implements`, `extends`) are MEASURED and REPORTED but not enforced — their derivations are incomplete (`implements` reads 26 truth edges against 444 emitted, which indicts the rule, not the analyzer), and enforcing an incomplete oracle produces a gate that cries wolf. `--strict` enforces them for whoever works on them. `calls` is the one label this gate does not touch: it has its own F5 differential, whose truth lives in the SHARED harness, and the consolidation merges replaced that oracle with a smaller one that lost its `:only` (CLJ-D21) and positional-refer (CLJ-D24) mirrors. Restoring it belongs in the shared file and is blocked on that file's churn.

design_decision.description: Clojure analyzer contract (CLJ waves, probe-verified 2026-09-19 against the pinned @yogthos/tree-sitter-clojure 0.0.14 wasm): the RULINGS below are load-bearing — each names the node types whose handling they govern.

decisions.question: Is `#Name[…]/#Name{…}` a constructor or a tagged reader literal?
decisions.resolution: RULED: shape + capitalization heuristic (AST cannot resolve classes): vec/map payload with a final UPPERCASE segment emits instantiates from the enclosing context (line = the tag name); anything else is reader DATA and its payload is NEVER walked as code (`#my/tag (call-x)` emits no call). Fixture tagged-ctors + mutants tag-payload-call/tag-lowercase-ctor.

decisions.question: Do reader conditionals trap code (cljc portability)?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the wrapper is transparent — children (`(expr)` bodies inside #? / #?@) are walked generically, so calls inside reader-conditional branches resolve; the wrapper emits nothing itself.

decisions.question: @x, #'f, and `~x`-style symbol-value reads: call edges?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NOT calls — a var quote/`sym_val_lit` names a var, a deref reads a value; none fabricate call edges (the member-access exclusion family, EX2 parity).

decisions.question: Literal containers as parameter/call sources?
decisions.resolution: RULED: containers are data positions — they emit no edges themselves; map_lit participates ONLY as a destructuring binding source in extractParams (:keys/:strs/:syms/:as/{local :key}; :or values are expressions, skipped). Fixture params + mutants param-body-leak/param-amp-kept.

decisions.question: Metadata positions and auto-resolved keywords: execution or trivia?
decisions.resolution: RULED: metadata occupies NO execution position (executionHead skips meta_lit — the #881 head rule, formally widened by the meta-head fixture) and never becomes a call; auto-resolved marks (`::k`) carry no call semantics; a `^:private`-wrapped name still resolves through the `name` field (shape-probed). AMENDED (adversarial F5, 2026-09-19): enforced LITERALLY — the meta_lit SUBTREE is skipped in the walk; the previous code honored the head rule but walked metadata payloads, so `^{:doc (meta-fn)}` fabricated a call to meta-fn.

decisions.question: Method impls `(px [_] …)` inside reify/extend-type/extend-protocol/proxy/defrecord/deftype: calls or definitions?
decisions.resolution: RULED: DEFINITIONS — a direct list child of those forms is a method symbol owning its body's calls, emits NO call edge (the measured `use-reify -[calls]-> px` fabrication), and the parent form emits the implements/extends edges (extend-* source = the named TYPE; reify/proxy source = the enclosing context). Fixture extend-reify + mutants reify-false-call/reify-no-implements.

decisions.question: Top-level directive forms and def-initializer calls after the ns?
decisions.resolution: RULED: top-level `(require …)`/`(import …)`/`(use …)`/`(refer …)` parse through the same libspec handler as ns clauses (quoting_lit unwrapped; aliases registered, imports recorded, references edged at the libspec line); calls outside any function attribute to the NAMESPACE (meta.isTopLevel) — def/defonce initializers and deftest bodies included (deftest is a function symbol). Fixtures toplevel-forms/toplevel-calls + mutants directive-ignored/toplevel-call-dropped.

decisions.question: Which libspec shapes resolve, and which nested vectors are data? Prefix lists `[prefix [sub :as a]]`, refer lists `:refer [foo bar]`, imports `(java.util Date)`.
decisions.resolution: RULED (CLJ-F5): three shapes, one rule each — (a) a nested vec DIRECTLY AFTER a keyword is a NAME LIST (`:refer [foo bar]`, `:only`, `:rename`), data, skipped (M12 caught the first prefix-list implementation fabricating `ns -[references]-> prefix.foo` from `:refer` — the FP is the pin); (b) a nested vec in any other position is a PREFIX SUB-LIBSPEC: sub = first child, `:as` alias registered as `alias → prefix.sub`, and `prefix.sub` is a references target (real Clojure semantics; clj-kondo's vendored rewrite-clj uses the form, +367 truth edges on that corpus); (c) vector imports `(java.util Date UUID)` record the CLASS items as imports, never walked as calls (C14 class). Fixture prefix-require + mutant prefix-require-flat.

decisions.question: Which constructor spellings instantiate, and how is the class name read?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F14): `(->ClassName …)`, `(ClassName. …)`, and `(new ClassName …)` all emit instantiates from the enclosing context. The capitalisation rule is FINAL-SEGMENT uppercase (`->probe.recs.Rec`, `->p/Rec` — the old first-char test rejected both, contradicting this spec's own comment), targets resolve through aliases in all three spellings, the line is the class name's, and `new` carries the argument arity after the class. Fixture ctors + mutant ctor-qualified-dropped.

decisions.question: Are threading macro steps invocations, and with what arity?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F13): steps of `->`/`->>`/`some->`/`some->>`/`cond->`/`cond->>`/`doto` ARE calls with THREAD-ADJUSTED arity (written forms + the injected value = +1); bare symbol steps emit arity 1; builtin-headed steps follow the builtin policy (no call edge); `cond->`/`cond->>` alternate test/step — tests walk normally; `->>` is NOT a ctor idiom and must reach this rule (it starts with `->` and was silently eaten by the ctor branch on BOTH sides); `as->` binds explicitly and stays as-written. Fixture threading + mutant threading-step-dropped.

decisions.question: Is `(:refer-clojure :exclude [replace reverse])` a libspec?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F2): NO — the clause is data. Its `:exclude`/`:only`/`:rename` name-lists are VAR names; feeding them through the libspec handler fabricated `references -> replace` + an import of package `replace` on 43 corpus files (string.clj, and a `[comment]` variant that even flipped the comment walk). The clause is consumed without dependencies; the top-level `(refer-clojure …)` form is likewise data. Fixture refer-clojure + mutant refer-clojure-walked.

decisions.question: Which cljc/cljs alias forms register aliases?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F12): read-conditional requires unwrap at BOTH sites — ns-level `#?(:clj (:require …))` and clause-level `(:require #?(:clj [x :as y] :cljs [x :as z]))` — with the union of platforms (CLJ-D2 transparency); `(:require-macros …)` is an accepted require sibling (alias + references); `:as-alias` registers the alias for qualified-name RESOLUTION but emits NO references edge and NO import row (the lib is not loaded — the alias-only form appears in real cljc). Fixture cljc-aliases + mutant cljc-alias-dropped.

decisions.question: `(case k (a b) :r …)` — is a constant-group list an invocation?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F7): NO — data. Constant-position LISTS (even child indices ≥ 2) are groups of unevaluated constants and are never walked (`calls a` was fabricated from one); the scrutinee and the result expressions still walk (the `(helper)` result emits). Fixture case-constants + mutant case-constants-walked.

decisions.question: What evidence may flip the file-global comment-shadow flag (#881)?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F4): DEFINITION evidence only — `comment` as a def-family NAME, or in a binding-vector position (fn/defn params, let/loop/for/…). A DATA-position symbol (`{comment 1}` map key, a `case` leg, a data vector) does NOT shadow the macro; the old any-non-head-occurrence scan flipped file-globally on data and walked every `(comment …)` body as code (fabricated `calls parse-string` on clj-kondo analyzer.clj). The #881 fixture's two live shadows (a fn parameter and a let binding) are exactly the surviving shapes. Fixture comment-data + mutant comment-data-shadow-flip.

decisions.question: Which comment blocks attach as a form's doc?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial F11): a CONTIGUOUS block of `;;` comments DIRECTLY above the form (each comment starting exactly one visible row above the next; comment nodes carry their trailing newline, so all row comparisons are visible-row). A trailing comment on the previous form's line, a blank-line-separated header, and single-`;` notes do NOT attach. Fixture doc-blocks + mutant doc-trailing-attached.

decisions.question: CC1: which forms count +1 cyclomatic complexity? The lane counted only if/cond/when/case/for/loop/when-let/if-let — omitting the not/some variants of its own if/when family, condp, the conditional threaders and while (W23-a, review #2).
decisions.resolution: RULED (M49 CC1-c, 2026-09-20): one rule — every conditional/loop CONSTRUCT counts +1; the full family = if/if-not/if-let/if-some, when/when-not/when-let/when-some, cond/condp/case, for/while/loop, cond->/cond->>/some->/some->>. Clause nodes are not counted in clojure (case children are pairs, not nodes — the elixir lane counts stab_clause nodes where the grammar exposes them, EX-D10); try/catch/finally and and/or count nothing (declared; elixir omits try too); the JVM/TS per-entry granularity stays declared-divergent (EX-D10 precedent). The four conditional threaders are counted in the THREADING branch (which intercepts before the builtin check). A companion parity item exposes per-symbol complexity (symbol.complexity mirrors metadata.complexity, the ELXD15 shape). FAIL-proof: pre-fix the ten additions read 1 (file total 8); post-fix the fixture reads 2 each (total 18). Fixture complexity-forms + mutants complexity-policy-dropped, symbol-complexity-stripped.

decisions.node_type: sym_lit (bare head that names a clojure.core var)
decisions.question: Is a bare head that is a clojure.core var a call? The lane's contract says no (builtin/special forms never produce Calls), and the suppression set WAS a 437-name hand transcription — 368 core vars + 69 deliberate extras.
decisions.resolution: RULED (M60 deep round, 2026-09-28): the SET is DERIVED, not typed. script/m14/tmp/clj-core-derive.ts parses clojure/clojure's own src/clj/clojure/*.clj with the pinned wasm, keeps only the files whose ns/in-ns is clojure.core (or clojure.core.protocols / clojure.core.reducers), keeps only TOP-LEVEL def-family forms (an internal helper inside a defn body is not public API), and drops what the lane's own privacy rule calls private (defn-, ^:private, ^{:private true}). That yields 654 public vars; the 69 extras (special forms, uncurried interop statics, the clojure.string/clojure.test spellings) are kept deliberately. The list stays a CONSTANT so the analyzer stays a function of ONE file, and the derivation is the evidence a gate re-checks. WHY IT MATTERED, MEASURED: the F5 oracle IMPORTS this object by reference, so every name missing from the list was a MIRRORED fabrication the differential structurally could not see — 2,525 calls edges in the clojure corpus (30% of all 8,391), 999 in clj-kondo, 151 in core.async. After the derivation the unshadowed residue is 6 / 11 / 2 (script/m14/tmp/clj-gate-census.ts, 0 RESIDUAL on all three).

decisions.node_type: sym_lit in a binding position (name shadow, by reference)
decisions.question: A core-SHAPED name can be the file's own var. Is the suppression position-blind (a flag), name-blind (a span), or neither?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the existing order-aware, region-scoped shadow table becomes a (name, span) LIST and `isCoreCallSuppressed(name, pos)` is the single gate every suppression site uses. Three exemptions: (1) SHADOWED — the file binds the name at that point (def-family name incl. declare/defmethod/deftest, a protocol/interface signature, a param, a binding vector, a letfn spec); a def binds at its form's END because Clojure compiles a form when it reads it, which is why the ranges are order-aware; (2) REFERRED — a :refer/:only/:rename name is a confirmed external target; (3) not a core name. The (name, span) shape is load-bearing: a bare span declared every later head in a file shadowed by, say, a protocol signature named `seq`, and the first post-change F5 run read 26 MISSING / 11 UNEXPLAINED for exactly that. Measured recovery: 555 real in-file call sites in the clojure corpus, 64 in clj-kondo, 27 in core.async.

decisions.node_type: sym_lit (protocol/interface signature head, method-impl head, letfn spec head)
decisions.question: May the core-builtin gate sit on a DECLARATION?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. A signature, an impl and a letfn spec are declarations; the gate belonged only on call sites. The gate that sat there was a leftover from C9, whose real fix was the null-prototype alias table — `toString` was NEVER in the list, so the gate never fired for the prototype-pollution class it was written for. What it did instead was delete members: gvec.clj's (definterface ArrayManager …) declares array/alength/aclone/aget/aset and four of the five are core names, so the interface shipped with ONE method; (definterface … (identity [x])) shipped with none. The 723-name list would have swallowed get/key/count too. Pinned by fixture proto-members.

decisions.question: `%`, `%1`..`%N`, `%&` are parameter references, not callees. The test was `/^%(\d+|&)?$/` — the lane's last regex.
decisions.resolution: RULED (M60 deep round): the clojure lane is ZERO-REGEX. `isAnonArgShorthand` is a char scan, and the conversion is PROVED not asserted — script/m14/tmp/clj-regex-equiv.ts runs the regex and the scan over every sym_lit name in three corpora (633 files, 187,678 symbol nodes, 13,363 distinct names) plus a 42-case adversarial battery and reports 0 mismatches. reviews/regex-policy.md's clojure row and validation/m49/regex-debt-register.json's row are removed with the literal, so neither can become a ghost.

decisions.question: `(:use [lib :only (names)])` — is `:only` read, and is its name list a vector?
decisions.resolution: RULED: `:only` is `:refer`'s legacy twin and reads identically, and the name list is a LIST as often as a vector — `(:use [clojure.java.browse :only (browse-url)])` appears 16 times in the clojure corpus alone (clojure.java.javadoc, clojure.java.shell, clojure.pprint, the test tree). `:refer :all` has no name list and stays on the `[*]` items path, which is the honest whole-lib reading. Pinned by fixture lib-rules.

decisions.node_type: list_lit (a name list nested in a libspec vector)
decisions.question: Is a list inside a libspec site ever a call?
decisions.resolution: RULED: no, at ANY depth. The C7/C8 guard looked only at a LIST parent, so it covered `(java.util Date)` and the direct libspecs but MISSED a name list nested in a VECTOR spec — and once :only was read, that fabrication acquired a lib: `ns -[calls]-> clj.java.browse/browse-up` with isTopLevel. The rule is now "is any enclosing LIST a libspec site", which is what the rule always was. Pinned by mutant clojure/libspec-name-list-walked.

decisions.question: Same as CLJ-D21b, stated once for the whole site.
decisions.resolution: RULED: the libspec subtree is DATA. Mirrored in deriveClojureEdges.

decisions.question: `(declare a b)` interns a var. Is a forward declaration a symbol?
decisions.resolution: RULED: yes — a Variable with isForwardDeclaration, NOT an export (a forward declaration is not a definition, and publishing it made the declared name and its real defn two public Variables under one name, which the harness's duplicate-export invariant caught). `declare` is a core form, so before this wave it produced no symbol and no edge at all AND its names were not in-file declarations, leaving every later call with nothing to resolve to: 68 sites across the corpora (mutual recursion in the compiler, clj-kondo's compojure fixture, core.async's dispatch). Pinned by fixture lib-rules + two mutants (symbol dropped, export published).

decisions.node_type: list_lit (two ns forms in one file)
decisions.question: A file with two `(ns …)` forms has two namespaces. Is the refer table one map?
decisions.resolution: RULED: no — it is a POSITIONAL SEGMENT LIST, one per ns form, and the post-walk resolution pass reads the call site's byte offset (carried in a Map keyed by the edge's array index, so the published relationship keeps exactly the fields the store contract declares). A single mutable table is wrong in BOTH directions: keeping it resolves a first-namespace call against the second namespace's clause, and resetting it at the second ns empties it for the post-walk pass, which leaves even the first-namespace call bare. 45 two-namespace files in the corpora. A closed segment is never reused — almost every file opens with (ns …) at byte 0, so "close at 0, then open at 0" returned a zero-width span matching no position, and every :refer in the file stopped resolving (the refer-forms fixture caught it). Pinned by fixture two-namespaces, which pins both failure modes with the same referred name called from two places.

decisions.question: A renamed libspec: which half of the pair is referable?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the NEW name, and the pairing is POSITIONAL — a map literal's named children alternate key/value, so `{old new}` is (child 0, child 1) and the new name is the ODD child. Reading both makes the name Clojure deliberately UNBIND resolve to a lib, which is the shadowing :rename exists to prevent; a call to it is a genuine unresolved var and stays BARE. This was the declared F17 limitation, measured at 7 sites in clj-kondo and now closed. Pinned by fixture lib-rules.

decisions.question: What is the name of `(s/def ::kw …)`?
decisions.resolution: RULED: `:current-namespace/kw` — the reader qualifies `::` against the enclosing namespace, and the symbol was published under the literal `::kw`, so the spec had an identity no other file could reference. 15 sites in one metabase shard alone. Pinned by fixture two-namespaces + mutant clojure/auto-resolved-spec-name.

decisions.question: Is `^:private` on a TYPE declaration private?
decisions.resolution: RULED: yes — it is the same privacy contract W24-mr3 established for def/defn, and the type branches never read it, so a private protocol or record was published in the namespace's export surface. Pinned by fixture proto-members + mutant clojure/type-private-ignored.

decisions.node_type: sym_lit (a qualified name whose own NAME contains a slash)
decisions.question: `h2x//` — a metabase function whose name is `/`. Is the qualified name read by splitting the text?
decisions.resolution: RULED: no. The grammar already splits a qualified symbol into `namespace` and `name` FIELDS, and the analyzer was splitting the TEXT a second time, TWICE and differently: `"h2x//".split("/")` is `["h2x","",""]` so the generic-call branch published `…honey-sql-2/` while resolveQualified (slice after the first slash) published `…honey-sql-2//` — two answers for one call site inside one analyzer. Every qualified callee is now read from the head node's fields, so the three emission shapes (generic call, thread step, #() shorthand) cannot disagree. The shape is invisible to a 60-file draw: it needs a function whose name ends in a slash. Pinned by fixture qualified-names + mutant clojure/qualified-name-text-split.

decisions.question: Is `..` unconditionally a Java member-access macro?
decisions.resolution: RULED: no — it is a core MACRO, and clojure/core.clj DEFINES it: `(defmacro .. "form => fieldName-symbol …" …)` at L1677. In that file every later `(.. sc comparator (compare …))` is a call to the macro the file itself defines, which is exactly what CLJ-D18's shadow guard admits. The analyzer read it that way (the `..` case falls through to the generic branch and the gate decides); deriveClojureEdges' `.`-prefix branch fired first and dropped it, so the full-extent run over clojure/clojure read 1 unexplained of 6,871 truth edges — the analyzer right and the oracle wrong, the m49 W24 shape. Pinned by the full-extent lane.

decisions.question: Is a top-level `(defsomething name …)` a definition or a call?
decisions.resolution: RULED: a DEFINITION. Any def-like head (`def`, optionally followed by `-`/`_`) whose first argument is a symbol defines that symbol — a general rule, not a list, because 1,136 top-level definitions across the four corpora recorded NOTHING (no symbol, no `contains`, no export): `defcurried` 8 sites in clojure/core/reducers.clj (all ten of that file's core vars), `definline` 6 at core.clj:5580+, and 1,043 in metabase (`defsetting`, `defenterprise`, `defclause`, `deferror`, `defspec`, `defroutes`), including LOCAL macros no per-file analyzer could be taught (`def-aset`, `defblockingop`) and third-party ones (`defprotocol+`). A CORE-NAMED definition macro is NOT excluded — `definline` is a clojure.core macro, and the first version's core-name guard threw those away. The kind is INFERRED (Function when an arglist vector follows, else Variable) and stamped `isUnknownDefMacro`, so no downstream claim rests on it. A def-like NAME in argument position is still not a definition. F1's node-type census is structurally blind to this class: an unrecognized def form parses as a `list_lit`, i.e. a CALL. Fixtures def-like-heads; mutants def-like-definition-dropped, def-like-call-fabricated.

decisions.question: Is `(in-ns 'a.b)` a namespace form?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES. It is how a file loaded into a running runtime declares its namespace, and `currentNamespace` stayed `user` for it, so 484 definitions across 17 files were stranded on owner `user` with no `contains` and the wrong scope — the whole of clojure's own pretty-printer. It is an ABSENCE, not a wrong value, which is why no per-class claim could see it. Three rules: the name is a QUOTED symbol (a raw field read yields `'a.b`, a name nothing can refer to); the alias/refer tables are NOT reset, because `in-ns` switches namespace without re-running `ns`; and the namespace is resolved POSITIONALLY, since a file may switch part-way. Fixtures in-ns-forms; mutant in-ns-namespace-lost.

decisions.question: Is `(Class/.member x)` a call, or a member access?
decisions.resolution: RULED: a MEMBER ACCESS — two `uses` edges, the member at the form's arity and the class at 0. It used to emit `f -[calls]-> String/.toUpperCase`, a target that is not a symbol, not an export, and in no `contains`: a dangling relationship. Invisible to F5 by construction, because the `calls` truth derives calls, the analyzer emitted a call, and the two agreed on an edge pointing at nothing; 23 real sites in clojure's own tests. THREE spellings exist and only two are recognized: `Class/.member` (dot after the slash) and `Class./member` (dot before) — the fixture is what found the second missing, still emitting `calls -> java.io.File./getName`. The third, `Class/member`, is deliberately left a CALL: it is identical in shape to `str/join` and `clojure.string/trim`, so promoting it would fabricate a member access for every qualified call in the corpus. `Class.` with a trailing dot stays a constructor `instantiates`. Fixtures static-interop; mutants static-interop-dangling-call, static-interop-class-edge-dropped, namespace-qualified-promoted-to-member.

decisions.question: Which symbol does a `contains` edge point at when a name has several?
decisions.resolution: RULED: deterministically, and at the DEFINITION. It was 'whichever the walk pushed first', and push order is not source order — a protocol's methods are symbolized when the protocol is met — so 667 edges across the three corpora could land on the later declaration. A definition always displaces a NON-definition: a FORWARD DECLARATION (`(declare HEADER)` at gen_math.clj:16 then `(def ^String HEADER …)` at 119, and the edge claimed the namespace defines the var where it only promises to) and a SPEC ANNOTATION (`(s/fdef my-inc …)` at spec_syntax.clj:6 then `(defn my-inc [x] …)` at 13). The non-definition SYMBOL is still published — the graph needs a node for the call target, and `declare` skips core names — only the EDGE moves. Among candidates the earliest declaration line wins. Fixtures contains-owner, spec-name; mutants contains-points-at-forward-declaration, contains-points-at-spec-annotation.

decisions.question: Does a `user` owner count as a namespace?
decisions.resolution: RULED: yes, in BOTH the explicit and the implicit case, and the distinction I first drew was wrong. `(in-ns 'user)` DECLARES one, and the eight definitions after it in clojure/core/server.clj belong to it — 36 containment edges were lost there. A file with no `ns` form also interns into the ambient namespace, and `user` is its conventional name. The fixture pair in-ns-user / no-ns-fallback settled it in the direction OPPOSITE to the rule's original argument: withholding the membership while keeping the export is the one option that cannot be made consistent, because the export pass's own invariant fires with 'export does not resolve to a top-level symbol (membership rides Contains)'. A file that declares no namespace now PUBLISHES it as a Module symbol stamped `isImplicitNamespace`, which is what lets the invariant resolve anything at all. Fixtures in-ns-user, no-ns-fallback; mutants contains-user-owner-dropped, implicit-namespace-symbol-dropped.

decisions.question: Can a spec form's argument be a literal?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO — a spec form names a VAR, so its argument must be a NAME. `(s/fdef 1 :args)`, a clj-kondo corpus fixture for reader recovery, published a symbol literally called `1` beside a `contains` edge `spec-syntax->1`. A symbol named after a literal is not referable, so it is a placeholder identity in a table whose contract is that every name in it is. The malformed form falls through to the generic-call branch, which records the spec expression's own call relationships and nothing else. Fixture spec-name; mutant spec-name-literal-minted.

decisions.question: Which `case` children are unevaluated constant groups?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the LIST children in CONSTANT positions, with the parity computed over EXECUTABLE children only. A `comment` is a named child, so one comment shifts every later index and a real BODY lands on an even index and is skipped, taking every relationship inside it with it — metabase/dev/src/dev/kondo_ratchet.clj:343 has 10 named children because of one `;;`, so the body at index 8 was dropped and the `uses` edges at 348-349 vanished from the graph. The FIX NARROWED the rule, it did not remove it: a list-shaped trailing DEFAULT is still an expression (W23) and a list in a genuine constant position is still a group of unevaluated constants (F7). It was invisible because the differential mirror had the IDENTICAL bug — both sides agreed on a body that neither one walked, and two wrong implementations of one rule is not a check. Fixture case-comment; mutant case-comment-body-dropped.

decisions.question: Is a `#js` payload data?
decisions.resolution: RULED: its VALUES are code and its KEYS are data. ClojureScript compiles `#js {:year (.year a-date)}` to a JavaScript object LITERAL, and a literal's values are evaluated; the blanket 'payloads are data either way' rule dropped every call and member access in them, six real ones in metabase's util/time/impl.cljs:313-319. The discriminator is the TAG: `#js`/`#JS` is the one tag whose payload is a literal with evaluated values, while `#inst`, `#uuid` and every record/class literal take data (CLJ-D1). A map walks its values and a vector walks its elements; a key is a property name, not an expression. Fixtures js-literal; mutants js-literal-values-dropped, js-literal-keys-walked.

decisions.question: Can one name be exported twice under two kinds?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. `(s/fdef my-inc …)` then `(defn my-inc [x] …)` produced two exports named `my-inc`, one Interface and one Function, because the dedupe key is `name|kind` and the two differ in kind. The harness's own duplicate-name invariant caught it, and the invariant is right: a namespace exports each name ONCE. But a spec IS a public entity when nothing else claims the name — `(s/def ::email :string?)` and `(s/def my-spec :int?)` have no `defn` and must keep exporting — so the rule is CLJ-D33's: a real definition displaces the annotation, an annotation with no definition stands alone. Fixtures contains-owner, spec-name; mutant spec-export-duplicated.

decisions.question: A call to a name the STANDARD LIBRARY also defines, in a file that redefines it: core, or the file's own var?
decisions.resolution: RULED: THE FILE'S OWN VAR, and only from the point the defining form COMPLETES. The suppression gate asks 'is this bare head core or locally defined?' and the ORDER of that question is the ruling: (1) shadowed by a local definition -> publish the bare name; (2) referred -> publish the resolved target; (3) in the core list -> emit nothing. Asking (3) before (1) drops every call below a definition of a core-named function - 401 edges in clojure/core.clj. A def-family name's range starts at the END of its form, so the rule does not reach backwards. The shadow TABLE is built by a pre-pass that must NOT descend into `quoting_lit` or `dis_expr`: a name in def-name position inside a quote or a `#_` discard binds nothing, and a range minted from either runs to end-of-file and shadows a core name the file never redefined. Fixtures shadowed-core-name, mutants shadow-check-after-core-return / prepass-descends-into-quote / prepass-descends-into-discard / def-range-reaches-backwards.

decisions.question: Do aliases from a TOP-LEVEL `(require '[lib :as a])` resolve, and which libspec shapes are readable?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, and the QUOTE IS THE CONVENTION, not an exception - `(require '[lib :as a])` is how the quote is written in real code, so an alias timeline that reads only unquoted spec lists finds nothing. A top-level require's children ARE the spec VECS, where an `ns` form's CLAUSES hold them, so one spec reader serves both shapes. All three alias keys are read: `:as` and `:as-alias` as a keyword with a following name, plus the positional form of `:as-alias` (`:as-alias aset`), which has no `:as` keyword to read. A bare lib name registers no alias. Fixture quoted-require-alias, mutant top-level-require-aliases-ignored.

decisions.question: Is a special form a call when the file REDEFINES it?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. The special forms are a CLOSED SET and a special form is not a call, whatever a file does to the name. clojure/core.clj:4748 is `(defmacro fn ...)` - core.clj redefines `fn` as a bootstrap macro - so the CLJ-D39 shadow rule published every `(fn ...)` below that line as a call to the file's own var: 212 edges, all wrong. The check is consulted BEFORE the shadow rule, not after, and it tests the WHOLE head rather than a prefix, so `fnan?` stays an ordinary var. `NON_CALL_FORMS` cannot serve here: it is a list of macros and binding forms consulted by the uses/contains derivations, where a special form is still worth walking, and it lists `clojure.core/fn`, a spelling no head is ever written as. Fixture special-form-not-a-call, mutant special-form-treated-as-call.

decisions.question: Is `recur` a call, and may a `calls` edge run from a symbol to itself?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO to both. `recur` is a special form - it transfers control to the enclosing fn/loop and names no var - and a relationship whose source and target are the same symbol is not an invocation. The analyzer pushed `calls: f -> f` with `isRecursion: true` on every recur, manufacturing 18 edges in clojure/core.clj alone, every one `lambda_83_6 -> lambda_83_6` on a line whose head is `(recur ...)`, with a target that is a GENERATED name for an anonymous function and therefore not navigable. Recursion is a real fact and belongs on the symbol's metadata. Removing the edge took the F5 unexplained count 189 -> 104 and the analyzer's edge count 3237 -> 3144. Nothing reads `isRecursive` today; that dead-capability claim is recorded rather than papered over. An ordinary direct self-call is unaffected and still published. Fixture recur-is-not-a-call, mutant recur-self-edge-fabricated.

decisions.question: Does a name-based 'this is a macro / a binding form / a def head' list outrank the shadow table?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. The shadow table is consulted FIRST, so a macro the FILE defines is the file's own macro and calling it is a call; only a name that is still the language's is filtered by the lists. clojure/core.clj is the worst possible file for the opposite order because it IS clojure.core: it defines when-let at :1879, if-let at :1859, doseq, lazy-seq and loop, and calls them 29, 9, 12, 41 and 29 times, and the lists suppressed every one. Three groups are non-calls UNCONDITIONALLY, whatever supplies the name: a THREADING MACRO (transparent expansion - the arrow in `(-> x (f y))` is punctuation, and core.clj defines `->`), a DEF HEAD (a definition, which CLJ-D30 already gives its own class, and core.clj defines definline/defn-/defonce), and a LIBSPEC OR CLASS-CREATING FORM (a directive that invokes nothing, and core.clj defines require/import while clojure.core.proxy defines proxy). Fixtures shadowed-macro-is-called, mutants shadowed-macro-suppressed / threading-macro-treated-as-call / def-head-published-as-call / libspec-published-as-call.

decisions.question: Which names are special forms, and where does that list live?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the list is the analyzer's `CLOJURE_SPECIAL_FORMS` and it gates the analyzer's own generic-call emission, so the two sides can be compared instead of trusted. CLJ-D41's copy in the truth was WRONG: it listed `loop`, `loop*`, `letfn`, `letfn*` and `case`, which are MACROS rather than special forms. core.clj defines every one of them, and CLJ-D43 says a call to a macro the file defines IS a call, so the analyzer was right about all five and the truth was wrong. Meanwhile the analyzer could not see `fn*` (a compiler intrinsic with no public var, so the core-list gate never reaches it) nor `let` (shadowed in core.clj). Each side had the other's gaps. A language fact recalled from memory is not a language fact; the disagreement is what exposed it. Fixtures special-form-vs-macro, mutants special-form-emitted-as-call / macro-suppressed-as-special-form.

decisions.question: Is `#(f …)` a call to `f`, and is a placeholder like `%` a callee?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES and NO. `#(f …)` parses as an `anon_fn_lit` whose children are the body DIRECTLY - no list_lit, no `fn` head - so a walk that fires on lists never visits it, and 55 of the residual edges in this wave were calls written that way, since core.clj is written in the shorthand. The analyzer names the shorthand `lambda_<row>_<col>` from the node's own position, so the `fn` owner rule applies to it as well. `#(% 1)` is the mirror: it APPLIES its argument and calls nothing, and it has the identical node shape - so the head needs a NAME test against the anon-argument placeholders (`%`, `%1`..`%9`, `%&`) and not a shape test. Fixture anon-fn-shorthand-call, mutants anon-shorthand-call-skipped / anon-arg-placeholder-called.

decisions.question: Does the anonymous-fn shorthand have to apply the SAME head routing as the list path?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, in full. CLJ-D45 made the shorthand a call SITE, and this ruling makes it a call site that routes identically. `#(.getName %)` took the shorthand's head path and pushed `calls: lambda -> .getName`, while the plain `(.getName o)` correctly emits `uses: getName` - a call edge to a name that starts with a dot, is not a var in the file, is not an export, and is not resolvable. 19 such edges across the corpus. It was invisible to the differential because the truth ALSO files these under `uses`, so the two implementations AGREED on the ontology and disagreed only on whether the shorthand had been analysed at all - which is why this looked like an unresolved policy question and was not one. The analyzer's convention was already settled and already implemented on the list path; the shorthand simply skipped it. A static member through the shorthand carries the same second fact the plain form does, WHICH CLASS, so both edges are emitted. Fixing it moved the enforced `uses` gate from 2650 to 2685 edges, still 100.00% with 0 missed and 0 fabricated, and removed 19 fabricated `calls`. Fixture anon-fn-shorthand-call, mutant anon-interop-head-called.

decisions.question: Is a call whose enclosing owner cannot be determined still a relationship?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, and it is attributed rather than discarded. The truth's `push` dropped any edge whose `from` was empty, on the reasonable-sounding grounds that a relationship needs two ends. That silently deleted 43 calls across the corpus, and because the discard was silent each affected file read as a COVERAGE GAP rather than as a bug - the worst being test_cl_format.clj:611 `(foo 3.14159)` inside a `(simple-tests ...)` block, where the owner chain ran out and the edge was built and then thrown away. The fallback is the analyzer's own C8 rule, not an invention: a call outside any function attributes to the namespace IN FORCE, the load-time context that actually invokes it. Where there is no `ns` form the chain continues to Clojure's default namespace, which the analyzer spells `user`; pinning that second half matters specifically, because the obvious fix - stop at the namespace in force - still drops every call in a file that has no `ns`, which is the smallest instance of the bug and is not contrived. Fixture ownerless-call, mutant ownerless-call-dropped.

decisions.question: What is the SOURCE of an `implements` or `extends` edge?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the analyzer's `activeFunction` — the innermost enclosing FUNCTION form, else the NAMESPACE. `walk`'s owner is NOT it, because that tracks `def` as well as `defn` and a `def` creates a VAR, not a function. So a `reify` inside `(defn future-call …)` anchors to `future-call` (core.clj:7291), while a `proxy` inside a `def` INITIALISER has no active function and anchors to the namespace (instant.clj:162 publishes `clojure.instant -> ThreadLocal`, not the var it builds). Both showed as SYMMETRIC misses and fabrications — 122/122 and 7/7 — where the counts matched exactly and every key was wrong, which is the most misleading failure a completeness gate can have. The pre-existing comment asserted the opposite and was half right: written about `proxy`, applied to `reify`. I then 'corrected' the proxy superclass on the strength of ONE sample and made `extends` worse, 7 of 39 becoming 33, so the rule is recorded as a measurement and not a generalisation. Fixture type-relation-source, mutants reify-anchored-to-namespace / proxy-anchored-to-def-name.

decisions.question: Do a namespace's aliases survive an `ns` form with METADATA and a PREFIX LIST in its `:require`?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, and both shapes were unread. (1) `(ns ^{:no-doc true} clj-kondo…indent …)` puts a `meta_lit` where the name is expected, so the name came back as `^{:no-doc true} clj-kondo…indent`; the caller does `if (v) out.push({at, name: v, aliases})`, so a wrong-but-nonempty name kept the entry while a wrong-but-empty one would have dropped the ALIASES with it. (2) A PREFIX LIST `[clj-kondo…node [protocols :as p] [whitespace :as ws]]` was detected by asking whether its first child is a symbol — which a prefix list ALSO has — so it took the plain-spec branch, found no `:as` among a symbol's children, registered nothing, and never reached the prefix branch; that branch also read the nested specs off the PREFIX rather than off its siblings, which is not the shape clj-kondo writes. The measured symptom was an alias table of size 1 where two aliases existed. Fixing both takes `implements` from 96.62% to 98.65%. A related sub-rule: a libspec with no dot in its first segment is RELATIVE and resolves against the requiring namespace, so `[protocols :as p]` inside `…node.indent` means `…node.protocols`. Fixture type-relation-source, mutant prefix-list-aliases-dropped.

decisions.question: What aliases does `references` read, and what is the FROM of a reference in a file with no `ns` form?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the ALIAS TIMELINE, and `user` when there is no namespace in force. `deriveClojureReferencesTruth` read its aliases from `namespaceTimeline`, which only sees the `ns` form's clauses, so a TOP-LEVEL `(require '[clojure.java.io :as jio])` was invisible and core.clj:7267 published the bare unresolvable `references: clojure.core -> jio`. That is CLJ-D40's defect in a derivation CLJ-D40 never reached, and it was INVISIBLE while the shared alias table was also wrong about prefix lists - two errors in the same direction cancel in a diff. Separately, `nsAt` returns "" for a file with no `ns` form and the analyzer attributes those references to `user`, so 70 edges were published as `references||...`: a relationship with only one end, which is what the 'all extracted, resolved and emitted' contract exists to prevent. CLJ-D47 taught this fallback to `calls`; the halves having drifted is the same lesson as the alias tables - one language fact re-derived in four places, each copy drifting differently. Fixture references-user-ns, mutant ownerless-reference-dropped. Measured: references 92.28% -> 96.23%, with implements at 98.65% and extends at 97.44%.

decisions.question: Which function does a `calls`, `implements`, `extends` or `instantiates` edge belong to - and is that the same question as `walk`'s owner?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the analyzer's `activeFunction` - the innermost enclosing FUNCTION FORM - and NO, it is not the same question as `walk`'s owner. `activeFunctionOf` is derived ONCE at module scope and read by three derivations, because CLJ-D48 originally built it inside the type-relation derivation and `instantiates` was still reading `walk`'s owner, disagreeing on 299 edges. One language fact, two derivations, two answers: the same lesson as the four alias tables, and the reason it lives where the next derivation can find it. Four positions settle it. (1) A `defn`-family form takes its own name. (2) A PROXY or DEFTYPE METHOD is a function form and owns its body - `(run [] (AtomicLong.))` publishes `run -> AtomicLong`. (3) A `def` creates a VAR, not a function, so there is no active function and the edge falls back to the NAMESPACE; this is why the fallback here is `nsAt` and not `walk`'s owner, and why `??` was wrong - `activeFunctionOf` stores "" and `??` does not fall back on it, so `add`'s `if (!from) return` dropped 6 `extends` edges silently, which is CLJ-D47's empty-source bug for the third time in this file. (4) An ANONYMOUS FUNCTION is owned by its GENERATED name `lambda_<row>_<col>`, for both `(fn ...)` and `#(...)`; the form name `fn` was inferred from one core.clj sample and refuted by a fixture on its first run. MEASURED: implements 72.52% -> 100.00% (444/444, 0 missed, 0 fabricated) and extends 82.05% -> 100.00% (39/39, 0/0), both now ENFORCED rather than reported; instantiates 87.45% -> 99.33%. Fixture active-function-source, mutants def-sourced-as-active-function / anon-fn-owned-by-form-name / proxy-method-not-a-function.

decisions.question: Is a static factory call `Class/method` an `instantiates` edge?
decisions.resolution: RULED: IT DEPENDS, and the dependence is not decidable from one file. `(RecordToTestStatics1/create {:a 1})` at test_clojure/protocols.clj:291 is published as `instantiates` because `create` is that record's factory; `Integer/parseInt` is not, because it is an ordinary static method. Adding the shape unconditionally measured 99.62% -> 66.67% with 520 fabricated edges, which is the measurement that decides it: telling a record factory from a static method requires knowing that `RecordToTestStatics1` IS a record, and that is CROSS-FILE TYPE KNOWLEDGE a per-file derivation cannot have. Recorded rather than guessed; these 41 edges are the known residual of `instantiates` at 99.62%. The other interop positions are not in doubt and are routed as CLJ-D32 rules them: `Class/.member` and `Class./member` are member ACCESSES and are `uses`, `(Class. ...)` is a constructor and is `instantiates`, `->Class` is the ctor idiom and is `instantiates`.

decisions.question: Is a `proxy`'s class vector ever wrapped, and may a libspec carry metadata?
decisions.resolution: RULED: BOTH MAY, and the decoration is not part of the name. `(proxy ^{:clj-kondo/ignore [:discouraged-namespace]} [yaml/YAMLCodec] [] ...)` is the shape metabase writes, and it fails twice over: `node.namedChild(1)` is a `meta_lit` where the vector is expected, and the qualified symbol's PREFIX carries the metadata, so `yaml/YAMLCodec` produced the target `^{:clj-kondo/ignore [:discouraged-namespace]}/YAMLCodec` - not a type, unresolvable by anything reading the graph. Both the truth and the ANALYZER read the node text rather than the prefix's `name` field, so both were wrong and the fix is the same in both. This is the third time a reader's decoration has been mistaken for a name, after CLJ-D39's `^{:no-doc true}` namespace and CLJ-D50's quoted require.

decisions.question: Is a NAMESPACE-QUALIFIED defining macro a function boundary?
decisions.resolution: RULED: YES, and the test for it is a FUNCTION-BOUNDARY test, not a DEFINITION test. metabase defines thousands of functions with `mu/defn` (Malli's `mu`), so `(mu/defn do-with-resolved-connection-data-source ...)` has to be a boundary or the constructor at :283 inside its body is attributed to the namespace. Widening `isDefLikeHead` for this was tried first and is WRONG: that function answers 'is this a DEFINITION', `contains` uses it, and making `mu/defn` def-like added 14 missed containments on the small corpora and 1,948 on metabase while changing implements and extends by exactly nothing. The qualifier is a namespace and not part of the macro's name, so it is stripped inside `activeFunctionOf` alone. MEASURED: metabase `extends` 98.04% -> 100.00% and `implements` 98.80% -> 99.66%, with the small corpora unchanged at 100.00%. Two questions were being conflated, which is the same shape as CLJ-D51's two derivations disagreeing about one rule. THE ANALYZER HALF, WHICH WAS THE LAST RESIDUAL. The truth side got this first and the analyzer did not, so the two were at different versions of one ruling and exactly one edge (`reducible-chunked-rows`, metabase load_data.clj:131) survived a fix that closed the other. Every `defn`-family branch compared the WHOLE head against `"defn"`, so `mu/defn` and `mu/defn-` matched nothing — no symbol, no function boundary. That also means the analyzer was creating NO SYMBOL for those functions at all: metabase `contains` emitted 59,061 -> 60,177, so 1,116 functions that exist in the source were previously absent from the graph entirely. Both gates now PASS on both corpora.

decisions.question: May a DEFINING FORM carry metadata, and where is a containment anchored when it does?
decisions.resolution: RULED: BOTH MAY, and BOTH SIDES GOT IT WRONG IN THE SAME PLACE. When a form carries LEADING metadata the grammar folds the metadata INTO the list_lit, so it becomes namedChild(0) and pushes the head to index 1 and the name to index 2 (itself wrapped, as in `^:parallel complicated-test-1`). Every `namedChild(1)` read therefore returned the MACRO: the analyzer published `contains -> deftest` with no line, created no symbol for `complicated-test-1`, and missed a sibling form outright; the truth had the same fixed-index scan. Both sides now use one reader that finds the head past leading metadata and unwraps the name at the name position. Second half of the ruling: a CONTAINMENT IS ANCHORED AT THE FORM'S START, which with leading metadata is the line the `^{...}` is on, not the line the head is on - the truth said 1261 where the analyzer said 1260 for sql_tools/sqlglot/references_test.clj, because the analyzer anchors where the symbol's RANGE starts. For a form without leading metadata the two coincide, so this is a no-op elsewhere. MEASURED on metabase: contains 100.00% with 0 missed and 0 LINE-MISMATCH (was 2 residuals), and the analyzer gained 2 symbols it was silently not creating.

design_decision._description: Clojure analyzer contract (CLJ waves + the M60 deep round, probe- and corpus-verified against the pinned @yogthos/tree-sitter-clojure 0.0.14 wasm): the RULINGS below are load-bearing — each names the node types whose handling they govern. CLJ-D1..D16 are the original sixteen; CLJ-D17..D29 are the M60 deep round (2026-09-28), which is the first wave whose instrument was the DERIVATION of a shipped constant rather than a hand list: the core-suppression set is derived from the language's own source (CLJ-D17), the suppression gate gained two exemptions so the expansion could not trade one fabrication for another (CLJ-D18), and the declaration/identity/ns-clause surfaces were swept on four corpora (4,885 tracked .clj/.cljc/.cljs files, 4,252 of them in one repo). The round found 13 defect classes, one of which (the core list) had been invisible to every existing gate because the F5 oracle imports the list by reference — a MIRRORED fabrication is invisible to a differential whose truth side carries the same bug, which is the lane's recurring blind spot and the reason the gap note below now names the instruments rather than asserting cleanliness. THE RELATIONSHIP-CLASS WAVE (2026-09-30) closed the two labels F5 never compared: `uses` and `contains` had no oracle, no gate and no residual, while the lane reported 100% completeness — the harness documents why (a label the truth side does not derive cannot be compared), and the consequence was never written down. CLJ-D30…D38 are what making those classes measurable produced, plus the four remaining classes (`references`, `instantiates`, `implements`, `extends`) which are now MEASURED but deliberately NOT enforced until their derivations are complete, because a gate that fails on correct output gets muted and then catches nothing.
